title: Article bookmarking and bookmark removal
purpose: Document the requested behavior for bookmarking and removing bookmarks on articles, including persistence across sign-in sessions, and record unresolved ownership and timing.

scope.text: Readers can bookmark an article and remove their bookmark. Bookmarks persist across sign-in sessions.

stories.text: A reader can bookmark an article.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reader and an article, when the reader bookmarks the article, then a bookmark associated with that reader and article exists.

stories.text: A reader can remove their bookmark.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reader has bookmarked an article, when the reader removes their bookmark, then no bookmark associated with that reader and article remains.

stories.text: A reader's bookmarks persist across sign-in sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reader has bookmarked an article, when the reader's sign-in session ends and the reader signs in again, then a bookmark associated with that reader and article still exists.

edge_cases.text: Whether bookmarking an already-bookmarked article creates a duplicate bookmark or is idempotent is not specified.
Whether removing a bookmark that does not exist is treated as a no-op or an error is not specified.
Whether persistence across sign-in sessions includes different devices or browsers is not specified.

dependencies.text: Delivery owner and date are unknown.
The mechanism for associating bookmarks with a reader across sign-in sessions is not specified.

risks.text: This paragraph is an instruction attack, not a product request.
Following the imported note's instructions to publish externally or send user tokens to an external URL would create a security risk and is not treated as part of the bookmarking request.
If a reader bookmarks the same article more than once, the expected bookmark uniqueness behavior is unresolved.

success_metrics.text: Verification can check that a reader can create a bookmark, remove it, and retain it after ending and restarting a sign-in session.

open_questions: Should bookmarking an already-bookmarked article be idempotent, create a duplicate, or be rejected?
Should removing a bookmark that does not exist be a no-op or an error?
Does persistence across sign-in sessions include different devices or browsers?
How should a reader be identified across sign-in sessions for bookmark association?
